mn_northwest_bluff_boulders.blurb: A small cluster of basalt blocks scattered among the roped lines of the Northwest Bluff in Duluth's Ely's Peak, in a wooded, fairly secluded corner of the cliffs. The handful of boulder problems here are on the hard side, roughly V4 to V6. Around them sit short trad leads and top-ropes, from easy fifth class up through the 5.11s, with a lone bolted line. It is a quick walk in on a trail from the lot toward the tunnel, so it pairs well with a session on the neighbouring bluff, though it is not a destination for beginners.

mn_c_section.blurb: The central stretch of the crescent-shaped M&M Hill cliff near Crane Lake, on the Minnesota side of the border. It holds sport leads, mostly 5.8 to 5.11 with a single route a notch harder, and a couple of the Hill's tallest lines, reaching past 60 feet. A few of the easier routes are the area's best-known classics, so it suits climbers stepping up from the 5.8 to 5.10 range as much as those chasing the harder pitches. Upper and lower sections are reached by separate trails. Expect a quiet, remote feel with little company.
mn_c_section.parking_note: Leave the car in the gravel pit on Nelson Road, about 0.8 miles from where it leaves Crane Lake Road. Avoid parking along the narrow, sandy-shouldered road itself.

mn_quarry_boulder.blurb: One large block of quartzite sitting in a hollowed-out old quarry in Blue Mounds State Park near Luverne, hidden in trees close to the south parking area. Some sides have been landscaped to improve the landings. The fourteen problems cover the whole range: a few VB to V1 warm-ups, a solid middle of V2 and V3, and a short run of hard lines from V5 up to V10. It is a good stop for a mixed group, with an easy walk in of only a few minutes from the paved path.

mn_mystical_mountain_south.blurb: The southern half of the Mystical Mountain cliffs in the Wolf Ridge area on Minnesota's North Shore, near Finland. Climbs here are tall, up to about 120 feet, and almost all are trad leads with a couple of top-rope options. The grades span the whole range: one very easy route, a few 5.7 to 5.9 lines, and a cluster of 5.11 classics topped by a 5.12. Because of the height, top-roping needs a belay from above and rappelling takes full-length ropes. It rarely gets crowded, and suits experienced trad climbers.

mn_slicksides_pit.blurb: A pothole pit about 15 feet deep at Interstate State Park, beside the St. Croix River at Taylors Falls. The thirteen problems run from easy VB up to V6, with a bulge of V1 to V3 plus a few harder ones. The rock is smooth and polished, with treacherous slopers, small crimps and poor footholds, so the grades feel stiffer than the numbers. Several of the taller problems are popular as top-ropes as much as boulders. It is a short walk from the park office, and the park favours clean climbing without bolts.

mn_9_chimney_buttress.blurb: The busiest buttress on the Prairie Walls, an east-facing quartzite cliff in Blue Mounds State Park near Luverne. About a dozen trad and top-rope lines, running from 5.6 through the 5.11s, with most of the climbs in the 5.8 to 5.9 range and a couple of well-liked harder ones. Cracks and roofs make up much of the character. The easiest approach is by way of the neighbouring Saturday Buttress, and the gully behind the buttress is the walk-off, so avoid routes near it on busy days. Morning sun, evening shade.

mn_boulder_area_2.blurb: A pair of boulders in the trees along the Bur Oak Trail in Blue Mounds State Park near Luverne, reached by walking down the trail from the interpretive center. Thirteen problems, nearly all easy to moderate: a lone V0, then a block of V1 to V3 with just one at V4. That makes it a friendly place for newer boulderers or a relaxed warm-up. The setting is shaded by trees, though patches of sun can still make it warm on a hot day.

mn_bluff_boulder.blurb: A single boulder with a handful of problems, up a short side trail in the woods above Ely's Peak in Duluth. Thirteen problems, mostly V0 to V2 with the bulk around V2, and just two harder ones at V4 and V5, so it works for beginners and for a short evening session. Getting there takes roughly 15 minutes from the car: follow the trail toward the tunnel, join the loop trail and a bike trail, then climb a path marked with pink ribbons. The surrounding woods are old growth, and the rock is basalt.
